The main takeaway from our work is that
the current guidelines for the use of troglitazone and metformin are based on a very small number of studies, which are of questionable quality.

the use of troglitazone in the setting of sulfonylurea treatment does not appear to provide any additional benefit in terms of glycemic control or reduction in insulin requirements, and may be associated with an increased risk for liver injury.
the combination of troglitazone with a sulfonylurea is not more effective than metformin alone in improving glycemic control.
